questions.prompt: In Next.js 15, how do you read params inside a page component?

options.text: Make the component async and await params (it's a Promise)
Read params.id synchronously — it's a plain object

questions.explanation: In Next.js 15, params is a Promise. Make the component async and do `const { id } = await params`.

questions.prompt: Which exported function pre-renders dynamic pages at build time (replacing getStaticPaths)? Type its name.
questions.explanation: generateStaticParams returns the list of params to pre-render; it is the App Router replacement for getStaticPaths.

questions.prompt: For app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx, what is the type of params.slug?

options.text: string[] — an array of path segments
string — the whole path as one string

questions.explanation: A catch-all [...slug] matches one or more segments, so params.slug is a string array.

questions.prompt: Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: getStaticPaths is the App Router way to list params

questions.explanation: [id] is one segment, optional catch-all matches the parent too, and notFound() shows not-found.tsx. generateStaticParams (not getStaticPaths) is the App Router function.

questions.prompt: Match each folder pattern to what it matches.

pairs.right: Zero or more, including the parent

questions.explanation: Single, catch-all, and optional catch-all differ in how many segments they match; generateStaticParams pre-renders the listed values.

questions.prompt: Order how a pre-rendered dynamic blog post is served.

items.text: generateStaticParams returns the list of slugs at build time
Next.js pre-renders one static page per slug
A request for /blog/my-post is served the matching static HTML

questions.explanation: generateStaticParams lists the slugs, Next.js builds a static page for each, and requests are served the pre-rendered HTML.
